## Overview

The May 6, 2026 acceptance guide covers Checkout, Elements with PaymentIntents, and Direct API. Customers in Brazil use their bank app to scan a QR code or paste a Pix string. The November 7, 2026 capture links to the same three variants.

## One-time payment paths

- **Checkout**. The May guide requires all line-item Prices in BRL and one-time line items for one-time Pix. It distinguishes dynamic selection from manual configuration, where the examples include `pix` in `payment_method_types`. The hosted example uses `success_url` and the embedded example uses `return_url`. The setup and recurring subscription route is [[source-stripe-pix-automatico|Pix Automático]].
- **Elements**. The May guide creates the PaymentIntent on the merchant server, passes the client secret to Stripe.js and uses `confirmPayment`. Its server examples distinguish Accounts v2's `customer_account` from Customers v1's `customer`. The guide says Elements collects CPF/CNPJ for cross-border transactions whether confirmation is on the client or server.
- **Direct API**. The May guide creates a server PaymentIntent and uses `confirmPixPayment` for the customer’s QR flow. Its HTML form collects name, email and CPF for individuals or CNPJ for businesses under `payment_method.billing_details`. It describes the government tax-ID requirement for cross-border transactions. To display the Pix string or QR code yourself, the May guide uses `handleActions: false` and `next_action.pix_display_qr_code`.

The May Elements guide uses `payment_intent.succeeded` for fulfillment after payment. The Direct API return page checks the retrieved PaymentIntent status. Rendering or scanning instructions and a browser return do not establish payment success. The May guide’s live flow requires a Brazilian bank account with Pix enabled.

## May 2026 expiration by path

| Path | Documented behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Checkout | `payment_method_options.pix.expires_after_seconds` can be 10 to 1,209,600 seconds (14 days). The default is 14,400 seconds (4 hours). |
| Elements | The guide says the QR code expires 4 hours after creation. Stripe then sends `payment_intent.payment_failed`. |
| Direct API | Use `expires_after_seconds` for 10 to 259,200 seconds (3 days) from PaymentIntent confirmation, or an `expires_at` Unix timestamp 10 seconds to 3 days ahead. Setting both causes an error. If neither is set, expiry defaults to 4 hours from confirmation. |

The Direct API guide says `next_action` can echo the requested `expires_at` even when actual expiry differs. Use `payment_intent.payment_failed` to identify expiry. Customers cannot pay an expired code. The merchant can confirm with another payment method or cancel the Intent after expiry, or cancel the Intent before expiry.

## Testing and troubleshooting

The May guide documents a sandbox tax ID (`000.000.000-00`) and a hosted **Simulate scan** test page. The ordinary delayed-success, `succeed_immediately`, `expire_immediately` and `expire_with_delay` email patterns ignore configured expiry. The `fill_never` pattern follows the expiry configuration and generates `payment_intent.payment_failed`. See each variant’s **Test your integration** section and the May Elements **Error codes** table for exact inputs, responses and recommended actions.

payments-pix-accept-a-payment.text: Learn how to accept a Pix one-time payment, a common payment method in Brazil.
You can set `expires_after_seconds` to a value between 10 seconds and 1209600 seconds (14 days). The default is 14400 seconds (4 hours).
Valid values are from 10 seconds to 259200 seconds (3 days)
The Brazilian government requires that buyers provide a tax ID (CPF/CNPJ) when completing cross-border transactions.
Pix QR codes expire after 4 hours from creation.

payments-pix-accept-a-payment.Q1: The November 7, 2026 base capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix/accept-a-payment identifies Pix one-time acceptance in Brazil and links Checkout, Elements, and Direct API (new raw lines 5-15). It contains no detailed prerequisites or state transitions. The May 6 guide describes Brazilian buyers paying a BRL checkout through their banking app with a Pix string or QR code. The Checkout path uses a Session with BRL one-time line items; setup and recurring subscription are addressed through Pix Automático (old raw lines 12-44). The Elements and Direct API paths create a PaymentIntent on the merchant server. Elements captures CPF/CNPJ for cross-border transactions and uses generic client confirmPayment; Direct API documents explicit customer fields and confirmPixPayment to render instructions (old raw lines 223-227, 452-586 and 905-1033). Issuing or scanning the instructions does not establish payment. The shopper pays in the bank app and the merchant checks Intent status or payment_intent.succeeded. Expiry can yield payment_intent.payment_failed; for Direct API an expired code cannot be used and the merchant may confirm with another method or cancel (old raw lines 729-741, 1041-1065 and 1162-1179). source-stripe-pix-accept-payment.md now distinguishes the May expiry limits, cross-border collection and the November navigation.
payments-pix-accept-a-payment.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix/accept-a-payment, the November change is presentation/navigation only (new raw lines 9-15), without proof of substantive product change or deprecation. The historical May 6, 2026 limits in source-stripe-pix-accept-payment.md are now qualified by variant. Checkout's relative expiry runs from 10 seconds to 14 days (old raw lines 99-104); Direct API supports up to three days, with mutually exclusive relative and absolute options and a relative clock anchored to confirmation (old raw lines 1162-1175). Both have a four-hour default, and Elements describes four-hour QR expiry from creation (old raw lines 223-227). Preserve the cross-border CPF/CNPJ qualifier and explicit Direct API example fields (old raw lines 223-225 and 905-937), the one-time BRL versus mandate-based setup/subscription split (old raw lines 14-35), and test simulation expiry exceptions (old raw lines 182-208 and 1134-1160). Keep the Stripe index route at line 359 and Real-Time Payments reciprocal route at line 207, add the source backlink, and label the November raw as a navigation reference. The dedicated Pix concept and its distinct subscription guide remain a route for dated recurring behavior.

concept_suggestions.anchor: **Integration**: Checkout, Elements, Direct API. Checkout supports setup mode and subscription mode (redirects to Pix Automático for recurring — unique among real-time methods). `expires_after_seconds` configurable (default 4 hours, max 14 days) via `payment_method_options.pix`. Tax ID (CPF/CNPJ) required by Brazilian law — Elements captures automatically; Direct API must collect explicitly.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown: **Integration**. The May 6, 2026 guide documents one-time Pix using Checkout, Elements or Direct API. Checkout’s configurable expiry is up to 14 days, Direct API’s is up to three days, and Elements describes four hours from QR creation. The guide gives CPF/CNPJ requirements for cross-border transactions. See [[source-stripe-pix-accept-payment]] for integration details and the separate Pix Automático route for setup or recurring payments.
